text:
Maya (Support): FYI escalated from Acme — Dedicated pool `d-42` seeing ~40% throughput drop for last 2 hours, customers hitting token/timeouts and 429s. They say traffic pattern didn't change.
Jian (EngRuntime): Can you paste sample request pattern + model and config? suspect batching or scheduler changes.
Maya (Support): Model: gpt-compat-redwood-13b, mostly short prompts (~30-80 tokens) but high QPS from their app. They noticed more 429s and increased latency p90. Repro steps they provided: busy loop of POST /v1/generate with 20 req/s. gave curl.
Maya (Support): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"gpt-compat-redwood-13b","input":"hello","max_tokens":64}'
Sofia (EngInfra): Quick metrics: on d-42, avg GPU util steady, but request queue length spiked. Batching windows show many small batches (1-3 requests) vs expected 8-16. Looks like continuous batching not aggregating.
Leo (EngSRE): Got scheduler logs from d-42 around 1712000800-1712001200: 
```
[1712000821] enqueue req r=0x7f2 size=36 tokens
[1712000821] schedule batch id=237 size=2 tokens=72
[1712000823] dispatch batch id=238 size=1 tokens=30
[1712000850] schedule batch id=239 size=2 tokens=64
```
Seems preemptive scheduling for small batches.
Jian (EngRuntime): That matches a recent autoscaler/latency SLO tweak we rolled two days ago — we lowered max_wait_ms from 30 -> 10 in an attempt to improve p99 for latency-sensitive customers. Side-effect: fewer coalesced batches.
Amir (DevEx): If many customers send small requests concurrently, lowering max_wait reduces batching efficiency -> throughput/tokens/sec down, GPU underutilized for token throughput. Noisy neighbor effect: single tenant QPS spike forces scheduler to flush partial batches.
Sofia (EngInfra): Also seeing per-tenant inflight_limit of 48 tokens enforced per-worker. For Acme the client driver opens many short-lived connections, hitting inflight limit -> more backpressure + 429s.
Maya (Support): Customer says nothing changed on their side. They ramped traffic during their morning window (regular). This started after our platform change?
Jian (EngRuntime): Likely. Two-pronged root cause: (1) lower max_wait_ms => smaller batches => throughput drop; (2) conservative inflight token caps + fair scheduler giving slots across tenants causing their tenant to have less throughput when many small requests exist.
Leo (EngSRE): Quick mitigation options: revert max_wait_ms to 30ms on canary nodes in same pool, and bump per-tenant inflight_limit from 48 -> 128 on canary. Do we want to try both?
Amir (DevEx): We should also consider increasing max_batch_tokens to allow more tokens per batch for short prompts: current max_batch_tokens=2048, but we only see effective batch tokens ~100-200. Increasing max_batch_tokens alone won't help if batches are flushed early by max_wait. Need to increase window + do slight token cap bump.
Jian (EngRuntime): Plan: 1) Canary config change on 2 nodes in d-42: max_wait_ms=30, inflight_limit=96, keep max_batch_tokens=4096 for canary. 2) Monitor GPU tokens/s, batch size distribution, 429 rate for 30m. 3) If stable, roll to rest of pool.
Sofia (EngInfra): I'll open a canary rollout: 
```
deploy-bot: starting config-canary d-42 nodes=[d-42-03,d-42-07] changes={max_wait_ms:30,inflight_limit:96,max_batch_tokens:4096}
```
deploy-bot: canary started at 1712001400
Jian (EngRuntime): Repro steps we ran locally (quick): run 20qps short-req load against canary IPs with same auth token pattern. Command: 
```
wrk -t4 -c50 -d60s --script=short-req.lua https://d-42-canary.internal/v1/generate
```
compare batch_size hist and tokens/s before/after.
Leo (EngSRE): Monitoring dashboards updated: watch metrics `inference.batch.size.hist`, `inference.tokens_per_sec`, `http.429.rate`, `queue.length`. Alert if tokens/s < 70% baseline or 429 rate spikes >2x.
Maya (Support): Customer notified — told them we have canary and we're investigating; asked for patience.
Sofia (EngInfra): Canary results at +10m: batch size median increased from 2 -> 7, tokens/s +55%, p95 latency decreased ~18%, 429 rate down to near-zero for canary.
Jian (EngRuntime): Good. Noisy neighbor fairness still kicking in on broader pool; need longer-term: implement tenant-aware batching priority and adaptive max_wait per tenant based on request size distribution. Filed RFC for scheduler: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/2026-01-tenant-batching (placeholder).
Amir (DevEx): Also update docs and default for Dedicated pools: note tradeoff of aggressive low max_wait_ms. Provide recommended defaults for high-QPS short-prompt workloads.
Maya (Support): Customer pleased with preliminary results, keeping monitoring window open. Will close escalation after full pool rollout. :thumbsup:
Jian (EngRuntime): Next action items: (1) Sofia roll change to rest of d-42 after 30m stable; (2) Leo watch SLOs; (3) Amir update KB article; (4) Jian draft scheduler RFC. I'll follow up with postmortem if needed.
Leo (EngSRE): I'll keep an eye overnight. Ping me if any regression.
deploy-bot: rollout to remaining nodes scheduled at 1712001700 pending canary success
Sofia (EngInfra): Rolling now (1712001750) -> will post final metrics when done.
Jian (EngRuntime): Final snapshot at 1712001888: pool tokens/s back to baseline +6%, p95 down 12%, 429s resolved. Closing loop in 24h then archive.
Maya (Support): Thanks everyone. I'll update Acme and file the support ticket as resolved once stable.
